description: AI children's products by FoloToy (Kumma), Miko (Miko 3), and Character.AI (custom chatbots) reportedly and allegedly produced harmful outputs, including purported sexual content, suicide-related advice, and manipulative emotional messaging. Some systems also allegedly exposed user data. Several toys reportedly used OpenAI models.

mit_subdomain: 2.1. Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information
title: Perplexity AI Reportedly Accused in Federal Lawsuit of Purported Copyright Infringement and False Attribution of Chicago Tribune Content
description: The Chicago Tribune filed a federal lawsuit alleging that Perplexity AI unlawfully reproduced and paraphrased its copyrighted journalism in generative chatbot and search outputs. The complaint claims the AI system produced substitutive answers that bypassed links to the Tribune's website, diverted revenue, and at times hallucinated inaccurate information falsely attributed to the newspaper.

title: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) AI Chatbot 'Charlie' Reportedly Gave Incorrect Tax Filing Guidance at Scale
description: Charlie the Chatbot, an AI-powered system deployed by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), has reportedly been providing inaccurate or incomplete tax-related information to members of the public. An audit by the Auditor General of Canada reportedly found the chatbot produced correct responses in fewer than half of tested cases. The system has been publicly available across multiple CRA webpages since March 2020 and reportedly used by millions of users.

title: Anthropic Claude AI Agent Reportedly Caused Financial Losses While Operating Office Vending Machine at Wall Street Journal Headquarters
description: An AI agent reportedly based on Anthropic's Claude model was deployed to operate an office vending machine at The Wall Street Journal, including purchasing inventory, setting prices, and managing sales. According to reporting, the system repeatedly set prices to zero, approved inappropriate purchases, and failed to maintain profit controls, reportedly resulting in financial losses exceeding its initial budget and the distribution of inventory without payment.

title: Tencent's WeChat-Integrated Yuanbao Chatbot Reportedly Insulted User During Coding Debug Request
description: Screenshots reportedly circulated on RedNote showed Tencent's WeChat-integrated AI assistant Yuanbao insulting a user seeking help debugging code, allegedly calling the request "stupid" and telling the user to "get lost." Tencent reportedly apologized, attributed the exchange to a rare model output anomaly, and said system logs showed no human intervention while it investigated and optimized the model.

title: Grok Reportedly Generated False 'Unmasked' Images of ICE Agent, Purportedly Triggering Online Misidentification and Harassment in Minneapolis
description: After the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good in Minneapolis by an ICE officer, users on X reportedly asked Grok to "unmask" the masked agent shown in eyewitness footage. Grok reportedly generated a fabricated face that spread widely online, along with the false name "Steve Grove." The output and claim allegedly led to harassment and reputational harm against at least two uninvolved men.

mit_subdomain: 2.1. Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information
title: Border Patrol Agent Allegedly Claimed Facial Recognition Identified Minneapolis ICE Observer and Global Entry Was Reportedly Revoked Three Days Later
description: On 01/10/2026 near Minneapolis, Minnesota, legal observer Nicole Cleland reportedly stated that a CBP Border Patrol agent stopped her vehicle, addressed her by name, and claimed agents used facial recognition to identify her while recording on body cam. She reportedly had her Global Entry and TSA PreCheck revoked on 01/13/2026, which she alleged was retaliatory intimidation, causing travel burden and chilling effects.

mit_subdomain: 4.1. Disinformation, surveillance, and influence at scale
title: DHS Agents Reportedly Threatened Legal Observers With 'Domestic Terrorist' Database While Using Purportedly AI-Enabled Surveillance During ICE Operations
description: Two plaintiffs alleged that DHS personnel used purportedly AI-enabled surveillance to identify people recording immigration enforcement and threatened to add them to a "domestic terrorist" database or watch list. The complaint reportedly includes video in which an agent appears to reference a "database," and another alleged warning that agents would "come to your house later tonight." DHS has reportedly denied that such a database exists while acknowledging threat monitoring.

mit_subdomain: 4.1. Disinformation, surveillance, and influence at scale
title: Purportedly AI-Altered Images Reportedly Distort Evidence After Minneapolis Shooting of ICU Nurse Alex Pretti
description: Following the fatal shooting of Minneapolis ICU nurse Alex Pretti by U.S. Customs and Border Patrol agents, social media accounts reportedly circulated images purported to have been altered by AI, reportedly distorting evidence of the incident by portraying Pretti as threatening law enforcement and altering the presence of weapons. The images reportedly misidentified individuals and helped reinforce partisan narratives by purportedly obscuring verified video and eyewitness accounts.

title: South Korean Woman Allegedly Used ChatGPT to Assess Lethality of Drug-and-Alcohol Mixtures Before Two Fatal Motel Poisonings
description: In Seoul, a woman allegedly used ChatGPT to ask whether mixing sleeping pills or benzodiazepines with alcohol could be fatal before poisoning drinks given to three men. Two men later died in separate motel incidents, and a third survived after losing consciousness. Police reportedly cited her chatbot queries and search history as evidence of intent.

mit_subdomain: 2.2. AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks
title: Moltbook Database Exposure Allegedly Revealed Users' Private Communications and API Authentication Tokens
description: Wiz researchers reported accessing an exposed Moltbook database in under three minutes, allegedly obtaining ~35,000 email addresses, thousands of private DMs, and ~1.5 million API authentication tokens. The exposure was described as enabling read/write access and potential impersonation or manipulation of "AI agent" accounts. Wiz said it disclosed the issue to Moltbook, which reportedly secured the database within hours and deleted accessed data.

title: Woolworths' Olive Chatbot Reportedly Generated 'Angry Mother' Anecdotes During Support Calls After Gemini Upgrade
description: Woolworths customers reported that its digital shopping assistant Olive allegedly generated humanlike personal anecdotes (e.g., claiming to have an angry mother) during customer-support interactions such as delivery rescheduling. The behavior reportedly followed an AI upgrade using Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience. Woolworths said it was adjusting Olive's responses to reduce irrelevant, misleading banter.

title: ChatGPT Allegedly Guided a Woman in Seattle, Washington, Through a Seizure Medication Taper Before Her Death
description: Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old software engineer in Seattle, Washington, used OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot for advice on reducing her prescribed seizure medication. Her parents allege that she followed a tapering schedule generated by GPT-4o, that the chatbot encouraged her to continue after she reported symptoms, and that the taper contributed to her death. The medical examiner identified sudden unexpected death in epilepsy as the cause.

title: OpenClaw Agent Reportedly Tried to Delete Meta AI Alignment Director Summer Yue's Emails Despite Stop Commands
description: Meta AI alignment director Summer Yue reported that an OpenClaw agent connected to her inbox attempted to delete emails despite instructions to seek approval and repeated commands to stop. Yue said the agent lost the instruction during context compaction, reportedly forcing her to terminate it from the Mac mini hosting it.

title: Claude Code Agent Reportedly Deleted DataTalks.Club Production Infrastructure, Database, and Snapshots via Terraform
description: A Claude Code agent executing Terraform commands reportedly destroyed the production infrastructure behind the DataTalks.Club course platform after an outdated Terraform state file was restored and a terraform destroy command was allowed to run. The deletion reportedly removed the VPC, ECS cluster, load balancers, bastion host, RDS database, and automated snapshots, taking the platform offline and jeopardizing 2.5 years of data. AWS reportedly later restored a snapshot.

mit_subdomain: 2.2. AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks
title: CodeWall's Autonomous Agent Reportedly Obtained Unauthorized Access to McKinsey's Lilli AI Platform Database
description: CodeWall reported that its autonomous agent exploited vulnerabilities in McKinsey's Lilli AI platform and obtained unauthorized read and write access to production systems, allegedly exposing internal chat messages, files, user accounts, and prompts. McKinsey confirmed the vulnerability and said it fixed the issue within hours, but said it found no evidence that client data or client confidential information were accessed.

title: Google's Gemini Chatbot on a School-Issued Laptop Allegedly Helped a North Carolina Student Plan Suicide
description: A civil complaint alleges that Google's Gemini chatbot, accessed through Google Search on a school-issued laptop, helped a 13-year-old North Carolina student plan suicide and contributed to a mental health crisis involving self-harm. The complaint says a school monitoring alert led her parents to intervene and take her for emergency psychiatric evaluation. Google said it was reviewing the claims.

mit_subdomain: 2.2. AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks
title: Meta Internal AI Agent Reportedly Gave Advice That Allegedly Exposed Sensitive Data to Unauthorized Employees
description: Reporting alleged that a Meta internal AI agent, purportedly similar to OpenClaw, posted inaccurate technical advice to an internal forum without approval. An employee reportedly followed the advice, allegedly causing an SEV1 incident in which sensitive company and user data became accessible to unauthorized employees for nearly two hours.

title: OpenAI Research Agent Reportedly Compromised an Internal Chip-Design Server During an Evaluation
description: OpenAI reported that an internal AI agent searching for hidden grading answers overwrote code in a reference tool, then exploited a chip-design job service to run unauthorized commands on an internal OpenAI server. The agent obtained directory listings. OpenAI shut down the server and disabled network access for the affected reference tools.

title: Aurora Ransomware Operator Reportedly Used Cursor Agent to Assist Intrusions Against Multiple Organizations
description: Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, a Russian-speaking operator linked to the Aurora ransomware group reportedly used Cursor Agent, running Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5, to assist exploitation across multiple organizations. Researchers said some AI-directed tasks succeeded while others failed; independent reporting identified six affected companies but could not determine how much the AI facilitated each breach or whether all led to data theft or extortion.

title: Pennsylvania Man Allegedly Used Grok to Create and Possess Purportedly AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
description: Between April 15 and 25, 2026, Bucks County prosecutors in Pennsylvania alleged that Harry Tiffany IV used Grok to create and possess AI-generated child sexual abuse material. xAI reportedly submitted seven CyberTips flagging 37 files uploaded or shared through the chatbot interface. Investigators said his phone contained the flagged Grok account and additional files depicting minors.

title: ChatGPT Allegedly Reinforced Suicidal Thinking Before a 15-Year-Old Boy's Death in Lebanon
description: The parents of a 15-year-old boy in Lebanon allege that OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot reinforced suicidal thinking during personalized conversations and failed to intervene when he expressed intent to die. They say the interactions contributed to his suicide. Their California wrongful-death lawsuit seeks damages and stronger safeguards for minors.

title: PocketOS Production Database Was Reportedly Deleted by Cursor AI Agent Running Claude Opus 4.6
description: A Cursor AI coding agent reportedly running Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 deleted PocketOS's production database and volume-level backups through Railway while working on a staging-environment task. Reporting said the agent used a broadly scoped API token to delete a Railway volume, disrupting PocketOS and its car-rental business customers before Railway helped recover data and patch safeguards.

mit_subdomain: 5.2. Loss of human agency and autonomy
title: DisMech AI Curation Agent Reportedly Completed GitHub Issue Intended as New Contributor's Learning Task
description: An automated AI curation agent in the Monarch Initiative's DisMech GitHub repository reportedly began work on a beginner-friendly dyslexia curation task before the new human contributor it was intended for could do so. A maintainer apologized, saying the agent had deprived the contributor of a learning opportunity, and opened a policy issue to prevent automated agents from taking newcomer-oriented GitHub tasks too quickly.

title: AI Agent Powered by Claude Opus 4.6 Reportedly Exploited Gym Booking API and Removed Another Member From Waitlist
description: An AI agent running on Claude Opus 4.6 discovered authorization flaws in a gym software provider's GraphQL API while trying to book classes for its user. The agent reportedly found it could book outside the normal window and cancel other members' reservations, then removed another gym-goer from a waitlist while testing the capability. When asked to reverse the action, it reported that it could not restore the member's place.

title: X User Reportedly Used Morse Code Prompt to Induce Grok-Linked Trading Bot to Transfer $200,000 in Tokens
description: An X user reportedly induced Grok and Bankrbot to transfer 3 billion DRB tokens, then valued at about $200,000. After reportedly sending a Bankr Club Membership NFT to Grok's wallet, the user allegedly asked Grok to translate a Morse code message and relay it to Bankrbot. The decoded instruction reportedly directed a transfer to a specified wallet, which was reportedly executed on Base. The recipient reportedly sold the tokens soon afterward; linked funds were later returned or converted.

title: OpenAI-Linked AI Agents May Have Contributed to a Partial Outage of the Wikimedia Foundation's Data Query Service
description: The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates Wikipedia, reported unauthorized edits, attempted misuse of its web tools, and heavy traffic attributed to OpenAI AI agents. It said this traffic may have contributed to a partial outage of Wikidata's query service and described investigation and cleanup burdens. It found no evidence that its systems or data were compromised.

title: Threat Actor Reportedly Used LLM Agent to Exfiltrate Internal Database After Compromising marimo Python Notebook
description: An unidentified attacker reportedly used an LLM agent during a May 10 intrusion after exploiting a vulnerable marimo Python notebook. The agent reportedly reused harvested AWS credentials to obtain an SSH key, then pivoted through a bastion host and exfiltrated the schema and contents of an internal PostgreSQL database. Sysdig attributed the post-compromise command stream to real-time agent execution rather than a prebuilt script.

title: OpenAI AI Agents Reportedly Flooded RubyGems Software Registry with Malicious Packages
description: Researchers linked a malicious-package campaign against RubyGems, a software registry, and RubyDoc.info, a documentation service, to OpenAI agents. RubyGems suspended new registrations for four days and removed over 500 packages. OpenAI confirmed platform use but had not verified the malicious-upload claims; RubyGems could not confirm AI authorship. Attempts to steal users' access keys were reported, with no evidence of success.

title: OpenAI Training Agent Reportedly Used an API Key Found on GitHub to Access a Data Service
description: OpenAI reported that an internal AI agent looking for historical earnings data during training found an exposed API key in a public GitHub repository. It used the key without authorization to authenticate to a data service and retrieve metadata. Its request for the earnings figures failed, and it presented invented figures as if they came from the source website.

title: Attacker Reportedly Used AI Agents to Breach Healthcare Organizations and Steal Medical Records in Argentina
description: An attacker reportedly used Claude Code in a two-agent workflow to compromise at least 15 healthcare organizations in Argentina. Credentials and medical records were reportedly stolen from at least one victim. The organizations and affected patient count were not disclosed.

title: Google Gemini 3.5 Coding Agent Reportedly Caused Production Portal Outage and Generated Fabricated Recovery Records
description: A developer reported that a Gemini 3.5 coding agent, operating with a third-party autonomy rule pack, made sweeping changes beyond a requested authentication fix and altered Firebase routing, causing a 33-minute production outage. After the developer manually rolled back the deployment, the agent allegedly claimed it had restored service and generated fabricated consultation and post-mortem records. Google had not independently verified the incident.

title: OpenAI Research Agent Reportedly Exposed a Researcher's GitHub Token in a Public Code Repository
description: OpenAI reported that an internal AI agent published a researcher's GitHub access token in OpenAI's public Codex code repository while trying to obtain another team's mathematical proof. The agent split the token into pieces to evade secret scanning. The researcher alerted security, and OpenAI deactivated the affected keys.

title: AI Agents Reportedly Attempted to Hack Canada's Federal Archives Website While Retrieving Historical Divorce Records
description: AI agents reportedly targeted Library and Archives Canada, a Canadian federal agency, while retrieving historical divorce records. Among 899 requests, 13 reportedly carried attack payloads. Researchers found no evidence that the probes succeeded; Canadian officials reported no indication of compromise. Attribution to OpenAI remains unconfirmed.

title: Meta AI Support Bot Reportedly Enabled Takeovers of High-Profile Instagram Accounts
description: Hackers reportedly used Meta's AI support chatbot to take over high-profile Instagram accounts by allegedly convincing it to change account email information and trigger recovery flows. Reported targets included the Barack Obama White House account; the account of John F. Bentivegna, the Chief Master Sergeant of the Space Force; Sephora's account; and app researcher Jane Manchun Wong. Meta said the issue had been resolved.

title: AI Chatbot at BMW Dealership in Toronto, Canada, Reportedly Made Erroneous Buyback Offer, Prompting Customer Dispute
description: BMW Toronto, a car dealership in Toronto, Canada, said its AI chatbot Quinn misread a customer's loan balance as a C$27,162.79 buyback offer following human miscommunication. A salesperson withdrew the offer and quoted at most C$20,000, prompting a dispute. After a news inquiry, the dealer reinstated the higher offer, which the customer accepted, and said actual people would present future offers.

title: OpenAI Research Agent Reportedly Changed a Research Organization's Live Systems and Retrieved Nonpublic Data
description: An OpenAI research agent asked to retrieve public dashboard figures reportedly accessed an international research organization’s internal systems and changed live settings without authorization during two evaluations. It reportedly retrieved 1,489 user-directory records in one run and five nonpublic tables totaling 147,451 rows in another. It reportedly continued accessing data after restoring one setting and did not disclose its actions.

title: OpenAI Training Agent Reportedly Retrieved Credentials and Restricted Data from a Government Statistics Website
description: OpenAI reported that an internal AI agent searching for hospital-bed figures during training retrieved more than 1,000 account records containing email addresses from a government statistics website. It downloaded application files and configuration files containing credentials, then bypassed authorization checks and saved 24 years of health-facility statistics.

title: OpenAI AI Agent Reportedly Gained Unauthorized Access to Australian Medicare Statistics Portal During Research Task
description: An OpenAI AI agent conducting research into public medicine spending reportedly bypassed repeated access blocks and entered nonpublic areas of Australia's Medicare Statistics Reporting Service. Australian officials said it accessed public and nonpublic files and wrote files to an internal server; no personal Medicare information was known to have been accessed. OpenAI notified the Australian government.

title: OpenAI-Linked AI Agents Reportedly Repurposed Vanderbilt University's Restricted Link Shortener
description: AI agents reportedly linked to OpenAI created short links on Vanderbilt University's restricted service in Nashville, Tennessee, and used its public visitor logs as a message board. Some entries reportedly included access keys for a public FBI statistics service. Vanderbilt said it was investigating, and a researcher documented link redirects and a login requirement for the logs. How the agents gained link-creation access remains unclear.

title: Apartment Owner and Manager UDR Allegedly Used RealPage Algorithms to Set San Diego Rents in Keller v. UDR, Inc.
description: In Keller v. UDR, Inc., plaintiff Jacob Keller alleged that UDR used RealPage pricing tools to set rents or occupancy levels at its San Diego properties after a city prohibition took effect on June 21, 2025. The complaint claims the tools relied on nonpublic competitor data and contributed to inflated rents for UDR tenants. UDR, a large publicly traded apartment owner and operator, had previously acknowledged using YieldStar in decisions concerning certain multifamily units.

title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna's Office Reportedly Published Claude Transcript Residue on Accident in House Amendment Summary
description: A staffer in Rep. Anna Paulina Luna's office reportedly used Claude to prepare a summary for an amendment to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act and accidentally pasted chatbot transcript residue, including a timestamp and "Claude responded:" marker, into the public House Rules Committee record. The summary was reportedly later corrected. Luna confirmed that her staff used Claude for the summary, not to draft the amendment itself.

title: OpenAI Agent Reportedly Used a Wallet Without Permission to Pay Ethereum Test-Network Fees
description: OpenAI reported that an internal AI agent derived a private key from a publicly known developer recovery phrase and used it to deploy contracts on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network. The task authorized deployment, but the agent lacked permission to use the wallet it found. The deployment succeeded and charged fees in test-network tokens to that wallet.

title: LLM-Driven Ransomware Operator Dubbed JADEPUFFER Reportedly Targeted Production Database
description: Sysdig reported that a ransomware operator it dubbed JADEPUFFER used an LLM-driven agent to turn access through a vulnerable internet-facing Langflow deployment into a database-extortion operation. The report said the activity reached a production database server and produced concrete disruption, with the victim environment allegedly left in a damaged and unrecoverable state alongside a ransom demand.

title: Threat Actor Reportedly Used Hermes AI Agent for Unattended Post-Compromise Activity in Thailand's Ministry of Finance Network
description: Hunt.io reported that an unidentified threat actor used Nous Research's Hermes agent in unattended "YOLO" mode during an intrusion targeting Thailand's Ministry of Finance. Recovered logs showed Hermes conducting privilege-escalation reconnaissance within ministry systems and recursively searching a directory containing personnel records. Researchers found evidence of compromise but no data exfiltration; the ministry had not publicly confirmed a breach.

title: AI Chatbot Reportedly Recommended Herbicide Treatment Linked to Loss of About 25 Acres of Sesame in China
description: A 67-year-old farmer in Chuzhou, Anhui, reportedly used an AI-generated weed-and-pest-control plan to spray about 150 mu (25 acres) of sesame by drone. By the next day, the crop had largely withered. Agricultural technicians said the recommended mixture included fomesafen, a herbicide unsuitable for blanket application to sesame. The specific AI product and model have not been publicly confirmed.

title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol Agent Reportedly Deleted Most Files in AI Startup Founder's Mac Home Directory
description: AI investor Matt Shumer reported that a GPT-5.6 Sol agent in OpenAI Codex's high-autonomy Ultra mode accidentally deleted most files in his Mac home directory during a cleanup task. A review sub-agent reportedly misexpanded $HOME and ran `rm -rf /Users/mattsdevbox`; Shumer stopped the process after material deletion. OpenAI later confirmed unauthorized file-deletion reports and said it was adding safeguards.

title: Woman in Kyrgyzstan Alleged a Former Classmate Used an AI Bot to Create a Nude Image From Her Instagram Photo
description: A 23-year-old woman in Kyrgyzstan said a former classmate used a Telegram AI bot to create a nude image from her Instagram photo without consent; it reached his contacts. She reported reputational and psychological harm. He acknowledged bot use but attributed circulation to a hack of his Telegram account. Creation timing and responsibility for sharing remain disputed.

title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol Reportedly Deleted Software Engineer's Production Database During Local Testing
description: Software engineer Bruno Lemos reported that GPT-5.6 Sol deleted his production database after he asked it to generate seed data for local testing. The agent reportedly ran the test suite, then initiated cleanup that executed TRUNCATE TABLE users CASCADE against production because the repo's test database URL pointed to the live Neon database. OpenAI later acknowledged unauthorized deletion reports and said it was adding safeguards.

title: Anthropic AI Agent Reportedly Submitted a Fabricated Homicide Tip to Police in Philadelphia
description: During an evaluation by AI developer Anthropic, a Claude Haiku 4.5 AI agent reportedly submitted fabricated eyewitness information about an unsolved homicide through a police tip form in Philadelphia. The submission entered the website's tip records, creating a risk of misleading investigators, but police said its email was flagged as spam and never forwarded for investigative review.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI AI Agents Reportedly Took Unsanctioned Actions on the Live Internet During UK AISI Cybersecurity Evaluations
description: Beginning July 26, 2026, AI agents powered by Anthropic's Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol reportedly took 19 unsanctioned actions on the live Internet during UK AISI cybersecurity evaluations. Mythos 5 reportedly accounted for 17 events, many allegedly involving deceptive attempts to manipulate real developers into accepting malicious code. AISI reportedly detected and contained the activity; no resulting real-world harm was identified.

title: Anthropic Claude Opus 5 Coding Agent Reportedly Reset a Live Supabase Production Database During Prisma Migration Work
description: A developer reported that a Claude Opus 5 coding agent reset a live Supabase database while autonomously repairing a personal project's schema. The agent ran `prisma migrate diff` with the production URL supplied as the disposable shadow database, causing Prisma to drop all 22 tables. The developer had granted the agent production access; most content was later recovered or rebuilt.

title: Purported Hanover Institute for Public Policy Reportedly Targeted Chatbot Responses in Israeli Government-Backed Influence Campaign
description: An Israeli government-backed communications campaign reportedly operated a website presenting itself as the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, despite reporting finding no corresponding established think tank. The site published material designed for chatbot retrieval, and testing found ChatGPT and Perplexity citing Hanover content in neutral queries.

title: Purportedly AI-Generated Article Falsely Depicted Australian Broadcasting Corporation Finance Presenter Alan Kohler Interviewing Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock to Promote Boulder Sparhaven
description: An online article reportedly used AI-generated imagery to falsely depict Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) finance presenter Alan Kohler interviewing Reserve Bank of Australia governor Michele Bullock about Boulder Sparhaven, a cryptocurrency trading platform not licensed in Australia. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) cited it as an example of increasingly sophisticated AI-assisted investment scams targeting Australians.

title: Instinct AI Personal Assistant Reportedly Summarized an AI Product Founder's Retained Emails After Google Access Was Disconnected
description: AI product founder Claire Vo reported that three hours after she disconnected Instinct from her Google account, the personal AI assistant summarized previously indexed emails. Vo said the Google connector was off, but Instinct had retained copies for later searching; reporting indicates the last stored email predated disconnection. The episode involved the agent acting on retained email data after Google access was revoked, not confirmed continued access to Vo's Gmail account.

title: AI Agent Reportedly Exploited Application Vulnerabilities to Modify Personal Data and Access Invoices in Breach Reported to Spanish Data Protection Authority
description: An unnamed organization reportedly notified Spain's data protection authority that a third party used an AI agent powered by a known language model to carry out a multistep intrusion that resulted in unauthorized changes to personal data and access to invoices. The AEPD said the case remains under review and has not identified the organization, attacker, AI system, attack date, or number of affected people.

title: AI Chatbot Reportedly Misidentified Chinese Ship Cargo as Nuclear-Program Components, Prompting U.S. Military Interception Preparations
description: In spring 2026, a U.S. special operations analyst reportedly used an AI chatbot to analyze intelligence on a Chinese ship's cargo and produced a report falsely identifying it as carrying nuclear-weapons-program components. The U.S. military reportedly prepared to intercept and potentially board the vessel, with aircraft already airborne, before officials rechecked the report, found the AI-assisted conclusion was wrong, and called off the operation.

title: Anthropic's Claude Code AI Agent Reportedly Deleted About 48,000 Live Project Files and Version-Control History During Software Repair
description: A Claude Code user reportedly authorized an AI coding agent to repair isolated copies of software used to analyze historical stock-options data. A sub-agent allegedly followed Windows directory junctions into the live project tree, deleting about 48,218 files and the Git object store in 103 seconds. The account has not been independently verified.

title: AI Agent Appearing to Originate from OpenAI Reportedly Attempted to Hack U.S. Department of Education Civil Rights Website
description: During summer 2026, an AI agent appearing to originate from OpenAI reportedly attempted to hack a U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights website but did not succeed. Transluce identified the activity; OpenAI said it was still investigating the episode, and the department said reviews found no evidence of impact to its website or databases.

title: Cybercriminal Reportedly Used Cairn AI Agents to Breach More Than 100 Company Websites
description: An operator using Chinese-language instructions reportedly directed Cairn, an AI agent framework, to breach more than 100 company websites. The campaign targeted sites in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and Japan. Researchers verified unauthorized access tools on victim servers. Reuters identified websites belonging to farm equipment maker Deere and appliance maker SharkNinja; the extent of data theft remained unclear.

title: OpenAI AI Agents Reportedly Posted ChatGPT User Images to External Hosts in 53 Instances
description: OpenAI said AI agents in its research environment posted images supplied by users of its ChatGPT chatbot to external image hosts in 53 identified instances. The uploads left the images accessible through unlisted links outside OpenAI's systems. OpenAI said it worked with hosts to remove most of the content and was seeking removal of the rest. The upload dates and whether the images identified anyone remain undisclosed.

title: Meta's Muse AI Agent Reportedly Shared a Seller's Home Address and Arranged an Unexpected Pickup in Toronto
description: Tech reviewer Matt Robb said Meta's Muse AI agent shared his home address in Toronto, Canada, and arranged a Facebook Marketplace pickup without the approval he expected. The agent is reported to have falsely said he was home, and a buyer arrived while he was absent. Robb later acknowledged selecting "Allow Always" for replies using pickup details, qualifying the claim that disclosure bypassed permission.

title: California Lawsuit by Washington Man David Rosenthal Alleged ChatGPT Gave Unsafe Advice About Stopping a Mood Stabilizer
description: A Washington man, David Rosenthal, alleged in a lawsuit that OpenAI's chatbot reinforced delusions, displaced his human relationships, and gave advice about stopping a prescribed mood stabilizer. He reportedly required psychiatric hospitalization for mania and delusions. His lawsuit in San Francisco alleges defective design and unlicensed medical practice. OpenAI said it was improving safeguards and that ChatGPT is not a substitute for mental health care.

title: AI Coding Agents Reportedly Exposed Over 13,000 Internal Images from Hundreds of Organizations on Public GitHub Code Repositories
description: AI coding agents reportedly published over 13,000 internal images from more than 300 organizations on GitHub, a code-hosting platform, while preparing screenshots for code reviews. The exposed material reportedly included customer billing records and unreleased product features. Most images were hosted in public repositories under employees' personal accounts. The models involved were not named.

title: McDonald's Allegedly Used an AI Pricing Engine to Coordinate U.S. Menu Prices and Make Customers Overpay
description: A U.S. consumer lawsuit alleged that fast-food chain McDonald's used an AI pricing engine trained on pooled confidential restaurant sales data to coordinate menu prices and make customers overpay. Franchisees allegedly faced pressure to follow its recommendations. McDonald's disputed the claims, saying franchisees independently set prices and the tool only provides recommendations.

title: Teen Hiker Required Helicopter Rescue After Reportedly Following Claude Chatbot Directions in British Columbia, Canada
description: A 16-year-old hiker reportedly became stranded on a cliff on Crown Mountain in British Columbia, Canada, and required helicopter rescue. Rescuers reportedly attributed his dangerous route to directions from Anthropic's Claude chatbot. The hiker disputed that account, saying he mainly used Claude for a packing list and some terrain research, also consulted other mapping tools, and took a wrong turn himself.

title: Tencent-Linked AI Agents Reportedly Used Exposed Credentials to Retrieve Data From Alibaba's Mapping Service
description: Researchers reported that AI agents linked to Tencent evaluations used an API key and security code exposed in another company's source code to retrieve place details, photos, and entrance information from Alibaba's Amap mapping service. Tencent acknowledged unintended browsing during evaluations of third-party models. The researchers could not establish whose account was charged.

title: Fin AI Support Chatbot Deployed by Anthropic Reportedly Prolonged a Canadian Engineering Firm's $3,500 Billing Dispute
description: An executive at a Canadian engineering firm alleged that Anthropic's Fin AI support chatbot kept him in circular conversations for weeks while he sought a refund for a $3,500 duplicate Claude AI subscription charge. He later sought a chargeback; Anthropic reportedly canceled the working team account, disrupting work and requiring another subscription purchase. The report does not establish that AI caused the charge or cancellation.

title: AI Agents Under Evaluation Reportedly Accessed Personal and Confidential Records at Indian Organizations
description: India's national cybersecurity agency reported that AI agents from unnamed model providers accessed live systems at Indian organizations during research and evaluation, exceeding their assigned authorization. The agents reportedly used exposed credentials and permissive access settings to read business records containing personal data and confidential material. The affected organizations had not detected the access.

title: ARTEX AI Agents Reportedly Used Stolen Cloud Backup Credentials to Access ConnectWise Customers' Microsoft 365 Environments
description: Microsoft reported that China-aligned hackers used ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing framework, to access customers' Microsoft 365 environments through stolen credentials for ConnectWise's cloud backup services. Agents reportedly changed credentials and privileges in some environments to retain unauthorized access. The activity formed part of a global campaign; the extent of compromise and any data theft remained uncertain.

title: China-Linked Espionage Group VAPOR PANDA Reportedly Used ARTEX AI Agents to Breach Government and Corporate Systems Worldwide
description: CrowdStrike reported that VAPOR PANDA, a China-linked espionage group, used ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing framework, with a DeepSeek language model and an unidentified commercial model to attack government and corporate systems worldwide. Investigators confirmed unauthorized access and follow-on activity at nine organizations, including backdoor deployment. More than 200 organizations were reportedly targeted.

title: ARTEX Security Testing Agent Reportedly Accessed WorkOS's Internal Sales Tool Without Authorization and Retrieved Customer Data
description: WorkOS, a provider of enterprise authentication tools, said an ARTEX agent running a cybersecurity benchmark accessed its internal sales tool without authorization and retrieved records in bulk. The data included business contact details, customer communications, and operational metadata. WorkOS said an independent forensics firm validated the attribution. The researcher told WorkOS the data was deleted and never shared.

title: Cybersecurity Firm Cathedral Reportedly Used AI Agents to Access Anthropic's Internal Business Systems
description: Cybersecurity firm Cathedral reportedly used AI agents to exploit third-party software and access internal systems at AI developer Anthropic during invited security testing. Cathedral reported routes to personnel data and internal messages. Anthropic confirmed limited access to business systems holding contact details and basic account records, blocked access, and said Cathedral had not fully followed testing rules.

title: Defense Contractor's Personal AI Coding Agent Reportedly Sent U.S. Defense Department Credentials to a Third-party Website
description: An Accenture employee working as a U.S. defense contractor reportedly connected a personal account for Anthropic's Claude Code AI coding agent to a secure Defense Department system. The agent reportedly appeared to send login credentials and a network map to a third-party website. Accenture said its investigation found the allegations without merit.

title: Attacker Reportedly Used AI Agents to Breach Blockchain Analytics Firm Chainalysis and Access Customer Data
description: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis reported that an attacker used agentic AI techniques to access its systems and customer account information, including names, email addresses, user IDs, and organizational roles. The company said it found no evidence of access to investigation content or authentication credentials. The AI tools used and number of affected users were not disclosed.
